notes.meaning: The psalm opens with a call to praise God both on earth and in heaven. His sanctuary refers to His earthly temple, while His mighty heavens points to the wide skies where His power and glory are clearly seen. All worship belongs to the Lord everywhere, from His earthly house of prayer to the highest heights of creation.

God's people are told to worship Him for two great reasons: what He does and who He is. His mighty acts include His power shown in creating the world, ruling over all things, and rescuing His people. His excellent greatness means His majesty has no limit, so our praise should match how wonderful He truly is.

A whole orchestra of wind, string, and percussion instruments is called to join together in joyful worship. Horns, harps, lyres, tambourines, flutes, and clashing cymbals were all used in Israel's festivals and temple worship. God welcomes the full sound of music, movement, and human skill to honor His name.

differ.view: These temple instruments belonged to Old Testament worship and were shadows that pointed to the spiritual praise of the heart in the church.
Believers are encouraged to use every modern instrument and expressive bodily praise to celebrate God with joy today.

notes.meaning: The call to praise reaches its peak by inviting every creature that has the breath of life to honor the Lord. Because God gave life to all breathing things, every breath should be used to give Him thanks. This joyful shout forms the final, ringing conclusion to the entire Book of Psalms.
